newsitem.title: UK: Europe LPG eases on mild weather, Mideast rallies.
newsitem.headline: Europe LPG eases on mild weather, Mideast rallies.

text.p: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices eased in Europe on high stocks and mild weather this week, but the Middle East rallied strongly as traders bid up for the second November Saudi spot tender, dealers said.
But they said Europe may have reached a floor because of an opening arbitrage window to Latin America and the U.S.

Middle East Gulf prices continued a bullish run on what some traders described as a speculative rally, since stocks in the major consumer markets of Japan and South Korea were high and winter demand had yet to begin.
Total U.S. propane stocks fell 1.7 million barrels last week to 48.7 million barrels, 16 percent below last year, and Algerian product continued to flow into the U.S. Gulf coast.

In Europe, propane cargoes traded this week at $256.50 cif France, $258.50 cif Sweden and $240.00 fob Flotta for a short into Petit Couronne. Butane cargoes were steady, with trades at $236.00-$238.00 cif NWE over the week.
In the Mediterranean, Algerian product sold into France and Morocco at $255-260 cif, in addition to the U.S. sales.
"Propane is being hampered by mild temperatures in Europe, but butane prices are strong in the Middle East," a trader said.
